headline.headline: BLUE JAYS BURY RED SOX, 6-0, AS SPRINGER GOES DEEP IN THIRD-INNING BURST
headline.deck: Toronto erupts for five runs in the third at Fenway, silencing Boston's offense completely.
headline.body:
BOSTON — George Springer crushed his 11th home run of the season as part of a five-run third inning that buried the Boston Red Sox, 6-0, Saturday at Fenway Park before 36,902 fans who had little to cheer about from first pitch to last. The Toronto Blue Jays' offense went dormant after that signature inning, but they didn't need another run — Boston's bats never generated so much as a threat against a Toronto pitching staff that shut out the Red Sox through all nine innings.

Springer's blast was the centerpiece of a rally that turned a scoreless game into a rout before Boston could blink. Cristopher Sanchez Lukes and Clement each contributed doubles in the uprising, and Andrés Monasterio added a stolen base as Toronto poured it on in a third inning that lasted long enough to deflate the home crowd entirely. The Blue Jays tacked on one final run in the ninth just to underscore the point.

The shutout loss stings more than usual in Boston today, because hours before first pitch the Red Sox front office confirmed a trade sending left-hander Connelly Early to the Washington Nationals in exchange for infielder Curtis Mead. The deal signals a franchise recalibrating its roster while its pitching staff and lineup both struggled to produce against Toronto. For the Blue Jays, the victory was their most complete performance in weeks.

secondary.headline: ROYALS STEAL DETROIT ON LATE RUNS IN NINTH
secondary.deck: Kansas City scores in the seventh and ninth to edge Tigers, 3-2, at Comerica Park.
secondary.body:
DETROIT — The Kansas City Royals scratched out single runs in the seventh and ninth innings to outlast the Detroit Tigers, 3-2, Saturday night at Comerica Park, handing winning pitcher Mize and reliever Waguespack the decision in a tightly contested 2:22 game before 32,867 fans. Detroit had held a 2-1 edge through six innings after plating a run of its own in the second and another in the fourth, but Kansas City refused to fold.

The Royals tied the game with their seventh-inning run, setting up a tense final two innings before delivering the go-ahead score in the ninth. The victory was a classic late-game execution by Kansas City, the kind of win that separates contenders from pretenders in a crowded American League Central race. Detroit now absorbs a painful home loss in a game it controlled for most of the evening.

secondary.headline: CALDWELL-POPE HEADS TO PHILLY AFTER GRIZZLIES BUYOUT
secondary.deck: Veteran guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope signs with the 76ers to chase a championship alongside LeBron.
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA — One day after the basketball world absorbed the seismic news of LeBron James committing to the Philadelphia 76ers, another veteran piece fell into place Saturday when Kentavious Caldwell-Pope agreed to a buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies and signed a one-year deal with Philadelphia. The addition gives the Sixers a proven, championship-tested wing whose defensive reputation and three-point shooting could prove invaluable in the conference semifinals still unfolding.

Rich Paul, LeBron's agent, acknowledged Saturday that his client rode an emotional roller coaster before finalizing his decision to join Philadelphia. Now the Sixers are wasting no time surrounding their new cornerstone with complementary pieces. Caldwell-Pope won a title with the Lakers in 2020 and brings a steadiness that younger rosters often lack. The 76ers are betting that this wave of transactions translates into playoff success before the current postseason concludes.

secondary.headline: TORTORELLA LEFT WITHOUT A BENCH AFTER VEGAS SHOWS HIM THE DOOR
secondary.deck: The fiery coach says he was disappointed by the Golden Knights' decision and is now searching for his next post.
secondary.body:
LAS VEGAS — John Tortorella, one of the most combustible and respected coaches in hockey, confirmed Saturday that he was disappointed by the Vegas Golden Knights' decision not to retain him following what he described as a surprising postseason run that nonetheless ended short of another Stanley Cup. Tortorella spoke candidly about being left without a job as the NHL second round continues without him behind a bench, saying he is hopeful his next opportunity arrives soon.

The move by Vegas sends a cold signal to coaches around the league: results alone do not guarantee job security. Tortorella's hard-nosed systems and willingness to challenge players publicly made him both admired and polarizing. Whatever team hires him next will inherit a proven winner with a track record of elevating rosters through accountability and structure. For now, one of hockey's most recognizable figures watches the playoffs from the outside.

column.headline: LEBRON IN PHILLY CHANGES EVERYTHING — AND THE NBA IS JUST NOW CATCHING UP
column.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers spent years lurking on the edge of relevance, drafting high, losing often and asking fans to trust a process that delivered heartbreak in roughly equal measure to hope. Now LeBron James is wearing their colors in the middle of a playoff run, and the entire architecture of the Eastern Conference has to be rebuilt around that fact. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope showing up less than 24 hours later is not a coincidence. Veterans smell what is being cooked in Philadelphia, and they want a seat at that table.

The rest of the league would be wise to stop treating this as a feel-good story and start treating it as a threat. LeBron has rearranged franchises before — Cleveland twice, Miami once, Los Angeles once. Each time, skeptics said the window was too small or the supporting cast too thin. Each time, they were largely proven wrong at least for a season or two. The 76ers are not a finished product, but they are no longer a punchline. That transformation happened overnight, and the conference semifinals will be the first real test of whether this thing has any teeth.

story.headline: CROW-ARMSTRONG POWERS CUBS TO 11-0 DEMOLITION OF PIRATES
story.deck: Chicago erupts for eight runs in two innings, shutting out Pittsburgh completely
story.body:
PITTSBURGH, July 25 — Pete Crow-Armstrong homered, doubled, stole a base and drove the Chicago Cubs to an 11-0 rout of the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday at PNC Park, a beating so thorough that Chicago did not allow a single Pittsburgh run across all nine innings before a crowd of 39,105.

The Cubs broke the game open with a five-run sixth inning after plating three in the fifth, turning a scoreless stalemate into a laugher in the span of two frames. Crow-Armstrong, who finished with his 23rd home run of the season, now carries a four-hit performance into Sunday's series finale as Chicago sits at 59-45, firmly in second place in the NL Central. Shortstop Dansby Swanson and Jose Ramirez each contributed doubles, and Ramirez joined Crow-Armstrong with a stolen base as the Cubs ran freely against a Pittsburgh defense that offered little resistance.

Starting pitcher Pete Skenes absorbed the loss for Pittsburgh after hitting Yan Gomes Amaya, and reliever Marinaccio, who earned the win, was not without blemish, plunking Seiya Suzuki. Still, nothing the Pirates threw at Chicago slowed the Cubs, who piled on a single run in the eighth to close out one of the most lopsided results of the weekend. Pittsburgh, now 53-52, has lost ground in the NL Central race and faces Crow-Armstrong and company again Sunday afternoon.

story.headline: LEBRON LANDS IN PHILLY, SHAKING NBA TO ITS FOUNDATION
story.deck: James joins 76ers in stunning move; Caldwell-Pope follows as Philadelphia remakes its roster
story.body:
LeBron James is headed to Philadelphia. The 41-year-old legend, still commanding the league's full attention after two decades, agreed to join the 76ers in a stunning free-agency decision that sent shockwaves from Cleveland to Miami and left the entire NBA scrambling to recalibrate. Rich Paul, James' longtime agent and confidant, confirmed Sunday that the road to Philadelphia was anything but smooth, describing the weeks-long process as an emotional roller coaster that tested even LeBron's famously unshakable resolve before finally landing on the City of Brotherly Love.

The seismic move triggered an immediate aftershock. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, freshly bought out by the Memphis Grizzlies, wasted no time aligning himself with James, agreeing to a one-year deal with Philadelphia to reunite with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate. The 32-year-old sharpshooter gives the 76ers a battle-tested, 3-and-D wing who has already won a championship alongside James, injecting the kind of winning pedigree that Philly has chased for years alongside Joel Embiid.

The fallout for teams left empty-handed is severe. The Cleveland Cavaliers, who made a passionate push to bring James home for a second time, now face urgent roster questions with a young core built partly around the hope of his return. Miami, where Heat president Pat Riley courted James with characteristic relentlessness, must pivot just as sharply. Meanwhile in Denver, restricted free agent Spencer Jones accepted a two-year, $12 million offer sheet from Oklahoma City, giving the Nuggets the option to match and adding yet another subplot to a July that has already rewritten the league's power structure entirely.

story.headline: GRANATO STEPS ASIDE AS CANUCKS SHAKE UP FRONT OFFICE AMID BUSY BLUE JACKETS DAY
story.deck: Vancouver's hockey trailblazer moves to adviser role as Columbus locks up Sillinger and Greaves
story.body:
Cammi Granato, the Hockey Hall of Fame forward who blazed trails on the ice for a generation of American women's hockey players, is stepping back from her day-to-day duties as assistant general manager of the Vancouver Canucks, transitioning into an adviser role within the organization, the team announced Sunday. Granato had been one of the most prominent women in NHL front office history since joining the Canucks' brass, but the front office shuffle signals a shift in Vancouver's organizational structure heading into the 2026-27 season.

While Vancouver reorganized, the Columbus Blue Jackets made two significant financial commitments on the same afternoon, locking up pieces of their rebuilding core. Forward Cole Sillinger, the 22-year-old center who has shown steady development since being selected 12th overall in 2021, agreed to a three-year deal worth $13.875 million, avoiding what would have been an arbitration hearing. Hours later, the Blue Jackets doubled down by signing goaltender Jet Greaves to a three-year, $15 million contract running through the 2028-29 season, betting heavily on the hometown netminder to anchor their crease through the heart of their competitive rebuild.

Meanwhile, former Golden Knights head coach John Tortorella, dismissed by Vegas following their surprising playoff run, told reporters Sunday he was disappointed by the organization's decision not to retain him but remains eager to return to coaching. The 67-year-old bench boss, who won the Stanley Cup with Tampa Bay in 2004 and coached the Flyers and Blue Jackets in recent seasons, said he expects to be behind an NHL bench again and is actively pursuing opportunities as the league's coaching carousel continues to spin deep into the summer.

story.headline: ROOKIE RECEIVERS RESHAPING THE NFC AS MINICAMP BATTLES HEAT UP
story.deck: First-round wideouts from April's draft are already turning heads in organized team activities.
story.body:
The ink has barely dried on rookie contracts across the league, but several first-round wide receivers from the 2026 NFL Draft are already forcing veteran starters to look over their shoulders during OTA sessions this month. In Minnesota, third-overall pick Darius Holloway out of Ohio State has been a daily highlight reel at Vikings minicamp, drawing raves from offensive coordinator Marcus Brady for his route precision and hands in traffic. Meanwhile in Atlanta, the Falcons' front office is watching closely as second-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr. develops instant chemistry with newly drafted wideout Terrell Simms, a 6-foot-3 burner from Georgia who fell to Atlanta at pick 11.

On the trade front, the New England Patriots made the boldest move of the spring by acquiring disgruntled Dallas Cowboys linebacker Micah Parsons for a package centered on two first-round selections and veteran guard Cole Strange. The deal, finalized last week, signals that first-year Patriots head coach Jerod Mayo is serious about rebuilding New England's defensive identity after the franchise posted its worst record in three decades during the 2025 campaign. Parsons, 26, is expected to anchor a retooled 3-4 scheme and immediately elevate a unit that ranked 28th against the run last season.

In the AFC West, the Kansas City Chiefs remain the standard despite their Super Bowl LX loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in February, and general manager Brett Veach spent the offseason aggressively addressing the offensive line. Kansas City signed veteran tackle Trent Brown to a two-year deal and used a second-round pick on interior lineman Javon Fields from Alabama, moves designed to better protect Patrick Mahomes after he absorbed a career-high 47 sacks in 2025. With training camp scheduled to open in late July, the Chiefs and Eagles appear on a collision course for what many analysts are already calling an inevitable Super Bowl rematch.
